title: Accelerator: SDKs — First 50 Minutes Playbook (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, time-boxed playbook for a new engineer or external integrator to get a meaningful Redwood SDK interaction running in the first 50 minutes. The idea: low friction, high confidence — finish with a working sample that exercises generate + streaming + an embedding call and a short checklist for production-readiness followups.

Audience:
- New hires (engineer, ML engineer, solutions eng) who need to ship an integration quickly.
- Customer engineers doing a PoC.
- Internal demo authors creating reproducible demos.

Constraints & design principles (quick):
- Keep the cognitive load minimal: 3 commands to install + 3 code blocks to run.
- Prefer copy-paste over deep explanation; footnote links for deeper reads.
- Exercise both text generation and embeddings in a single flow to showcase unit economics differences.
- Surface common failure modes early (auth, network, model mismatch).

First 50 minutes plan (timeboxed):
0–5m: Setup and expectations
  - Objective: By minute 50 you will have used the SDK to: 1) call a text model and stream output, 2) compute an embedding, 3) run a tiny latency experiment.
  - Preconditions: Python 3.10+, Node 18+ optional, API key ready (REDWOOD_API_KEY).

5–15m: Install and quick smoke test
  - Python (recommended for labs):
    $ python -m venv rwd-env && source rwd-env/bin/activate
    $ pip install --upgrade pip
    $ pip install redwood-sdk  # placeholder package name
  - verify env: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY
  - quick sanity script (save as smoke.py):
    from redwood import Client
    c = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
    print('ok', c.ping())
  - Expected output: 'ok' + brief status; if fails, check env var & proxy settings.

15–30m: Hello streaming demo (interactive)
  - Goal: show partial tokens arriving and how to cancel.
  - Example (pseudo-code, runnable):
    from redwood import Client
    c = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
    stream = c.generate_stream(model='rwd-medium-1', prompt='Write a 4-line haiku about platform reliability')
    for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk.text, end='', flush=True)
        if "latency" in chunk.text.lower():
            stream.cancel()  # demo cancellation
  - Teaching points: streaming reduces perceived latency; demonstrate cancel and partial outputs.

30–40m: Quick embedding + compare (cost/latency note)
  - Single call embedding to show vector workflow:
    from redwood import Client
    c = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
    v = c.embeddings.create(model='rwd-embed-1', input='Redwood inference platform quick test')
    print('len', len(v))
  - Compare: note that embedding calls are usually CPU-bound and cost-per-unit differs from token generation; surface console metrics after run.

40–48m: Tiny latency experiment + metrics
  - Run 10 sequential generate calls (short prompts) and measure: p50/p95 rough numbers.
  - Script idea: record start/end, compute average. Push a note to console about which region and model used.
  - Expected result: share approximate timings and point to Console -> Per-route metrics for correlation.

48–50m: Wrap up and checklist
  - Save your working directory as a reproducible snippet.
  - Safety: remove API key from shared logs.
  - Next steps: follow production checklist below if this is moving to a demo or PoC.

Short production-readiness checklist (follow after PoC):
- Pin model versions (no floating latest).
- Add retries with exponential backoff and idempotency consideration for side effects.
- Use streaming for UX-critical routes and batching for high-throughput routes.
- Enable prefix caching when prompts share stable system instructions.
- Add observability: per-route token breakdown, p95 latency, error rate dashboards.
- Run a small quality evaluation: 50 prompts + expected outputs -> regression alert.
- Confirm data residency/KMS for Private deployments.

Common issues and triage notes (from past onboardings):
- "Invalid API key" -> env var spelled wrong OR team key intended for Dedicated. Check console key scopes.
- Proxy errors in corporate networks -> set HTTPS_PROXY or run via cloud-shell.
- Model mismatch (tokenization edge cases) -> try a different model family, check sample token counts.
- Excessive cost during experiments -> run at low temperature, shorter max_tokens, enable quota alerts.

Ops tips for the facilitator
- Keep a short script to reset rate limits for demo accounts (support-only action).
- Pre-warm a small batch to avoid cold-start latency in the demo region.
- Have a fallback: a smaller local model or pre-rendered transcript if network is flaky.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (doc-level):
- Do we want a copy for Node-first audience with identical UX paths? (yes, create parity template)
- Create an official snippet bundle in the repo (one-dir runnable sample) and link it here.
- Add an appendix: how to interpret Console cost breakdown for embeddings vs generation.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this concise; aim for a single A4 sheet handout plus the repo.
- Consider a 20-minute trimmed variant for quick sales demos.

Appendix: suggested repo layout for the runnable lab (one-folder):
- README.md (objectives, prereqs)
- smoke.py (ping + quick generate)
- stream_demo.py (streaming code)
- embed_check.py (embedding example + small similarity check)
- metrics_run.py (tiny p50/p95 measurement harness)

End of sketch.

Revision history:
- 2024-09-12: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-09-18: added embedding notes (Ethan)
- 2024-10-02: clarified production checklist and unresolved TODOs (Priya)
